title: Sussex bus drivers announce three-day strike over pay dispute

tea.why: Drivers rejected a two-year pay offer, arguing it constitutes a real-terms pay cut compared to the current 4.2% RPI inflation rate.
tea.want: A fair pay rise that members find acceptable.
tea.changed: Nov 21: Unite announced that approximately 1,300 bus drivers will strike on December 1, 10, and 19.

summary: Approximately 1,300 bus drivers in Sussex, represented by the union Unite, have announced plans to strike on December 1, 10, and 19. The industrial action follows the rejection of a two-year pay offer from Go-Ahead, which the union claims amounts to a real-terms pay cut. The strikes are expected to cause significant disruption to Brighton & Hove Buses, Crawley Metrobus, and Spirit of Sussex services. Unite regional officer Jamie Atkinson stated that the company is responsible for the potential disruption and urged them to table a better offer. In response, Matthew Ashton, managing director for the bus operators, stated that the company remains committed to reaching an agreement and has requested further meetings with union representatives to resolve the dispute.
response: Matthew Ashton, managing director for the bus operators, stated the company has offered a pay deal that would increase driver pay by approximately 50% since June 2021 and has requested further meetings with the union to resolve the dispute.

updates.text: Unite announced that 1,300 bus drivers will strike on December 1, 10, and 19 following a rejected pay offer.
